speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Since you have multiple skin lesions, where exactly are they located on your body, and how long have they been present? Do you notice any changes in their size, color, or shape over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the daycare exposure and your brother's recent chickenpox, were these lesions present before or after your brother's rash appeared, and do you see any vesicles or scabs alongside the papules? Also, is the child currently afebrile?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum. The clinical presentation of pearly papules with central umbilication is pathognomonic, and the lack of vesicles or systemic symptoms makes chickenpox unlikely despite recent exposure.
